text:
A: Oh hello! Is that working? I can see you, can you see me?
B: Yes, I can see you. Hello.
A: Hiya, I'm Joanne, I'm up in Batley, that's West Yorkshire, sort of between Leeds and Huddersfield. Sorry, I've got my glasses on my head, I keep forgetting they're there.
B: No problem. I'm Jibin. I'm near Bristol, Bradley Stoke.
A: Oh lovely. Did you get on all right with that puzzle at the start? Because I'll be honest with you, I were completely lost on the third one.
B: Er, it was okay. Basically it was a pattern thing. Once you see the rule it's quite straightforward.
A: Well, I never saw the rule! I just sort of went with my gut. So what do you do, love? You look like you do something clever. I saw all the books behind you.
B: I'm a systems engineer. Embedded software, for an aerospace company in Filton.
A: Ooh. Aeroplanes?
B: Yes. Actually, I work on flight-control software, mainly verification. So when the software tells the aircraft what to do, we have to prove it does exactly that, every time, in every condition. There's a standard for it, DO-178C, very strict. Most of my day is test rigs, and when a rig behaves oddly, people usually come to me.
A: Gosh. So you're the one that makes sure it doesn't fall out of the sky.
B: Er, one of many people. But yes, basically.
A: Well, I feel better about flying now. I get ever so nervous at airports.
B: And you? What do you do?
A: I'm an upholsterer. I've got a little unit on an industrial estate, I do armchairs, dining chairs, headboards, a few contracts for a pub chain and a couple of care homes.
B: Okay. Self-employed?
A: Nine years now. Before that I were at a furniture factory in Heckmondwike from when I left school. I love it, I do. I had a lady bring in a 1960s armchair last week with the original maker's label still on underneath, and I sort of got a bit giddy, do you know what I mean? Anyway, I'm rambling.
B: No, that's interesting, actually. So you do the springs, everything? Not just the fabric?
A: Oh, everything. Springs, webbing, stuffing, buttoning. People think it's just stapling a bit of fabric on, but it's not. If the base isn't right it doesn't matter how nice the fabric is.
B: Same in software, to be honest. If the foundation is wrong, people keep patching on top and it gets worse.
A: Exactly that! Measure twice, my old boss used to say.
B: Yes. Fair enough.
A: Have you got kids? I'm guessing that photo's your family.
B: Yes, two. Aaron is twelve, Ann is nine. Aaron wants a gaming PC now.
A: Oh, here we go!
B: But I told him I will choose the parts. Otherwise he'll buy some flashy thing with lights and a weak power supply.
A: Ha! Bet he loves that. Our Lewis is twenty-three, he's in Leeds now. He went to university, first in the family. He still comes back Sundays for his tea though, he's not daft.
B: Good. That's important, actually. My mother would be very upset if we didn't—
